title: Setting Up Your Environment
description: Install Node.js, npm, and create your first React project using Vite.

data.text: Before building React applications, you need a development environment. This means installing Node.js (which includes npm), choosing an editor, and generating a project scaffold that you can run and edit.

data.title: Required Tools
items: **Node.js** — the JavaScript runtime that executes your code outside the browser.
**npm** — the package manager that ships with Node.js and installs React and other dependencies.
**Vite** — the recommended build tool and dev server for new React projects.
**VS Code** (optional) — a popular, free editor with excellent React support.

data.text: Download the **LTS (Long Term Support)** release from nodejs.org. LTS versions are tested, stable, and receive security updates for longer. After installation, verify everything works with `node -v` and `npm -v`.

data.title: Verify Installation
data.content: Check Node.js and npm versions in your terminal

data.text: Creating a React Project with Vite
Vite is now the recommended way to scaffold React projects. It is fast, minimal, and uses native ES modules. The command below creates a new project, installs dependencies, and prepares a dev server.

data.title: Create React App with Vite
data.content: Scaffold and run a new React project
data.code:
npm create vite@latest my-react-app -- --template react
cd my-react-app
npm install
npm run dev

data.title: Create React App Is Legacy
data.text: You may still see `npx create-react-app my-app` in older tutorials. CRA is slower and adds unnecessary tooling. Vite is the modern standard.
After creating the project, you will see a clean structure. The most important files are `index.html`, `src/main.jsx`, and `src/App.jsx`.

data.title: Default Vite Structure
data.code:
my-react-app/
├── node_modules/
├── public/
│   └── vite.svg
├── src/
│   ├── App.css
│   ├── App.jsx
│   ├── assets/
│   ├── index.css
│   └── main.jsx
├── index.html
├── package.json
└── vite.config.js

data.title: File Roles
items: **index.html**: The single HTML entry point. React mounts here.
**src/main.jsx**: Bootstraps React by rendering `<App />` into the DOM.
**src/App.jsx**: Your root component — the starting point for your UI.
**package.json**: Lists dependencies and scripts like `dev`, `build`, and `preview`.

data.text: `npm run dev` starts a local server, usually at `http://localhost:5173`. Changes to your code appear instantly thanks to Hot Module Replacement (HMR).

data.title: First Run Checklist
items: Open the URL shown in the terminal.
Confirm you see the Vite + React welcome page.
Edit `src/App.jsx` and watch the browser update.

data.title: Port Already in Use
data.text: If port 5173 is busy, Vite automatically tries the next available port (5174, 5175, etc.). Check the terminal output for the correct URL.

data.title: Recommended Extensions
items: **ES7+ React/Redux/React-Native snippets** — fast component and hook boilerplate.
**Tailwind CSS IntelliSense** — autocomplete for utility classes.

data.title: Exercise: Hello React
data.description: Create and run your first Vite React project.
steps: Install Node.js LTS and verify with `node -v`.
Start the dev server and open it in your browser.
Change the h1 in App.jsx to say your name.
data.expectedOutcome: A running React app with your name displayed in the browser.

items.question: Do I need VS Code?
items.answer: No. Any editor works (WebStorm, Sublime, Neovim). VS Code is recommended because it is free and has the best React extension ecosystem.

items.question: Should I use npm, yarn, or pnpm?
items.answer: All three work. npm is built into Node.js and requires no extra setup. This course uses npm for simplicity.

items.question: What Node version should I use?
items.answer: Use the latest LTS release. At the time of writing, Node 20 LTS is the safe choice.

items.question: Can I use a framework like Next.js instead?
items.answer: Yes, but this course starts with plain React and Vite so you understand the fundamentals before adding framework abstractions.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Install Node.js LTS to get npm and the JavaScript runtime.
Use Vite to scaffold new React projects quickly.
The dev server runs with Hot Module Replacement for instant feedback.
Keep your editor ready with React-friendly extensions.
data.takeaway: Your environment is ready. Next, you'll learn JSX — the syntax you will use for every React component.
